methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large international randomized phase III noninferiority trial (6,088 patients) comparing 3 versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine for high-risk stage II and stage III CRC, with regimen selected before randomization (CAPOX vs FOLFOX). The methods specify time-to-event endpoints (DFS/OS), Kaplan-Meier plots, and multivariable Cox models adjusted for prespecified minimization factors, with proportional hazards checked (Schoenfeld residuals) and restricted mean survival time used if proportionality failed. A clear noninferiority margin is stated (HR 1.13 for DFS/OS) and long follow-up with substantial event accrual is reported (1,255 OS events). Key operational details such as allocation concealment/blinding and missing-data handling are not described in the normalized manuscript excerpt.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual randomized controlled trial (3 vs 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy) and therefore maps to Oxford LoE 1b. The clinical question is directly practice-relevant because oxaliplatin neurotoxicity is duration-dependent, and the trial reports identical 5-year OS (82.4% vs 82.4%; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.86-1.07) while supporting shorter therapy. The regimen-dependent findings (noninferiority confirmed for CAPOX but not for FOLFOX) are clinically actionable for shared decision making in adjuvant CRC.

reporting_quality.justification: As a randomized phase III trial, CONSORT is the applicable standard, and the manuscript includes a CONSORT diagram reference, explicit endpoint definitions (DFS/OS), and key analytic details (Cox models with specified covariates; noninferiority testing; proportional hazards checks). The results report effect sizes with hazard ratios and confidence intervals for primary and key subgroup analyses. However, several CONSORT elements are not visible in the normalized text (eg, allocation concealment/blinding procedures, protocol deviations handling, and updated toxicity/QoL reporting are noted as not updated after the initial report). No data/code sharing statement is present in the provided text.

novelty_literature.justification: The core question (3 vs 6 months of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy) is established within the broader IDEA collaboration, and this manuscript largely provides extended follow-up focused on overall survival. The main added value is long-term OS confirmation of noninferiority with substantial follow-up and event counts, plus regimen- and risk-stratified OS results. This is a meaningful extension rather than a first-in-class concept.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with standard sections and defines key terms and endpoints (DFS/OS) in the Methods. Results are presented with quantitative effect estimates (HRs, CIs, and noninferiority P values) and figure captions that explain analyses (eg, Cox models with minimization covariates). The discussion is focused on clinical implications (eg, absolute OS differences and neuropathy tradeoffs) without obvious overstatement, though some details are deferred to appendices/supplement.

key_strengths: Very large randomized phase III noninferiority design (6,088 patients) with long follow-up and many OS events (1,255).
Clinically decisive OS finding: 5-year OS 82.4% vs 82.4% with noninferiority margin pre-specified (HR 1.13).
Appropriate survival methodology (KM, multivariable Cox with prespecified covariates) with explicit proportional-hazards checks and contingency RMST modeling.
Actionable subgroup framing showing regimen dependence (CAPOX supports 3 months; FOLFOX less clear).
key_concerns: Toxicity and quality-of-life outcomes were not updated beyond the initial report despite being central to the duration tradeoff.
Noninferiority was not confirmed for some subgroups (eg, FOLFOX-treated and higher-risk strata), so the 'most patients' recommendation needs careful boundary-setting.
Several CONSORT operational details (allocation concealment/blinding, missing-data handling) are not present in the normalized manuscript excerpt.
Data/code availability is not described in the provided text.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Given the scale, randomized noninferiority design, and clear long-term OS results with clinically meaningful toxicity implications for adjuvant CRC, this work is plausibly acceptable at a top oncology tier despite moderate novelty.
